title: Prove the evaluation can detect degradation before reporting any null
description: 5p00kyy/neuroterrarium hit our exact symptom and documented the way out. docs/PHASE3.md:66: 'Biological and all five shuffled controls each emit 20 total spikes, including 10 GF spikes, with identical mean-trace responses despite 502 to 561 changed target slots.' Their arms were indistinguishable. Rather than adding seeds they added coarse perturbations that must break anything -- no recurrence, all-excitatory signs, unit-contact weights, silencing the stimulated population -- which yielded 10/0, 20/10 and 0 spikes respectively. That established the evaluation could detect degradation, which is what turned their tie into a reportable null instead of a broken instrument.
design: We need the same ladder. Candidates, cheapest first: zero the frozen connectome weights entirely; flatten every Dale sign to +1; replace synapse counts with unit weights; silence the input population. Each should move the score measurably. If none of them moves it, the floor is in our harness and no arm comparison means anything. If they move it and real-versus-shuffled does not, the null is real and reportable. Note we already have partial evidence the arms are not degenerate: decision_window_v783.json records 2379 / 2570 / 6527 spiking neurons for real / shuffled / random, so our shuffle does mix -- unlike theirs, which they flag as possibly under-mixing ('Swaps are not a uniform sampler and preserve strong unique-weight connections').
acceptance_criteria: A perturbation ladder runs alongside the three arms, each rung's effect on score is recorded, and no null result is reported until at least one rung demonstrably degrades performance.
notes: Concrete template from cobanov/flyjump, docs/experiment.md:84-93, on 100 held-out seeds absent from training and validation: connectome + trained readout 99/100 completed at score 2885.75; same readout with the circuit silenced 0/100 at 41.00; initial untrained readout 0/100 at 41.00; handwritten rule baseline 0/100 at 535.27; uniform random 0/100 at 42.77; idle 0/100 at 41.00. Two rows carry the argument -- the same TRAINED weights with the substrate silenced, and the UNTRAINED readout on a live substrate -- because together they show both the circuit and the training are necessary. We have neither. Note their own limit, connectome-review.md:30: 'It does not demonstrate a biological topology advantage: matched MLP / rewired-graph training remains an open experiment.' And experiment.md:93: 'A topology-benefit claim would require matched artificial/rewired controls trained with equal budgets; that study is not included.' That study is ours.

title: Add an observation-ablation control: does the policy read its input at all?
description: liuzihe02/fly-craftax -- the project our controls.py cites for its liveness criterion -- ran this control and it overturned their result. From their tracker.md:107: replaying the trained readout with vision blacked out and with vision frozen left the action mix and score essentially unchanged, 27 and 22 achievements against 25 for the intact run, so 'the readout is not reading vision at all'. Their conclusion on their own trained policy: 'on this one seed the trained readout is best described as a clock with a small drive-dependent jitter, not a visually guided policy'. Separately, tracker.md:99: 'pure noop out-survives the wired fly (168 vs 155), so no adaptive control was shown'.
design: We have no equivalent control. If our three arms ever separate in score, the difference is uninterpretable until we know the policy conditions on the observation at all. Cheap to build on our side: evaluate the same trained policy with the observation replaced by a constant vector, with a frozen first observation, and with the substrate drive cut, and compare score and action distribution against the intact run. A policy whose score is unchanged under a blanked observation is a clock, and any arm ordering it produces is an ordering between clocks.
acceptance_criteria: evaluate_policy can run in blanked, frozen and drive-cut modes, the three comparisons are recorded in provenance beside the intact score, and no arm comparison is reported without them.

title: Our input is a tonic current; the reference model uses per-neuron Poisson with refractory disabled
description: Read from philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model, the reference our LIF parameters come from. Every LIF constant matches ours exactly -- v_0 -52, v_th -45, t_mbr 20, tau 5, t_rfc 2.2, t_dly 1.8, w_syn 0.275 -- but the input model does not. model.py:84-92 builds one PoissonInput per targeted neuron with N=1 and rate r_poi (default 150 Hz, model.py:39), weight w_syn * f_poi = 0.275 * 250 = 68.75 mV against a 7 mV rest-to-threshold gap, so each event forces a spike rather than charging the membrane. The next line is neu[i].rfc = 0 * ms, with the comment 'no refractory period for Poisson targets'. Ours applies a single constant 20.0 mV per step to all 1042 input neurons simultaneously, with the refractory period in force.
design: The reference has the same 1.8 ms delay inside the same 2.2 ms refractory period, so it does not avoid the collision numerically. It avoids it in two ways at once: independent per-neuron Poisson processes desynchronise the driven population from the first step, and the refractory period is switched off for exactly the neurons being driven. That is precisely what the two xfail(strict=True) markers in this repo prescribe -- 'the Poisson input the reference model uses, not a tonic current'. Note that gradient_reach_v783.json shows the gradient does reach the encoder on the real subset despite the tonic drive, so this is a fidelity question rather than a blocker. But the drive amplitude is also the knob that puts the random arm into runaway, and a forced-spike Poisson input decouples 'make the inputs fire' from 'how much charge enters the network'.
acceptance_criteria: Either the input is changed to per-neuron Poisson forced spiking matching the reference, with the choice recorded as a pre-registered amendment, or the deviation from the reference is stated explicitly in the write-up with its consequences argued.

title: Evaluation has no discriminating power until the policy is off the floor
description: Across sixty evaluation games at 600 training steps the raw variant scored -1.0 on every arm, and the standardised variant -1.0 / -0.9 / -0.9, i.e. one win in twenty on two arms. Zero episodes were truncated, so these are genuine losses against the scripted opponents rather than a mechanical hang. A comparison between arms cannot detect any difference while all arms sit at the floor, regardless of how many seeds or episodes are added.
design: Two independent questions this raises. First, what training budget lifts the policy off the floor at all -- worth finding by a coarse sweep on one arm before spending on three. Second, whether the scripted opponents (board_control_opponent, greedy_face_opponent) are simply too strong for any budget the compute allows, in which case the pilot needs a weaker opponent or a shaped signal, and that is a protocol question.
acceptance_criteria: A training budget is identified at which at least one arm wins a non-trivial fraction of evaluation games, or the opponent choice is revisited as a pre-registered amendment.

title: Choose the operating point in (drive, w_syn); the drive alone is the wrong knob
description: Measured on the real P1 subset at the restored 300-step window with the published w_syn, via controls.activity_profile with the real input and readout indices (data/results/drive_at_window_v783.json). At INPUT_DRIVE_MV = 20.0 the active fraction is 0.1762 for real, 0.2104 for shuffled and 0.6037 for random, against the 0.25 ceiling calibrate_w_syn uses as criterion 2. The real and shuffled arms pass; the random control is 2.4x over. Sweeping the drive, 0.2 is the only value tried at which all three arms pass -- random reaches 0.3655 by 0.5 -- and everything plateaus above 10, with 20.0 and 10.0 giving identical figures.
design: This is a confound rather than a tuning problem. The experiment's whole premise is that the arms differ in their edges and in nothing else, but at the production drive one arm sits in a qualitatively different dynamical regime from the two it is compared against: running away rather than transmitting, by the project's own definition. A difference in regime is a second explanation for any difference in score. 20.0 was chosen at the broken 30-step window where nothing propagated past the input population, so there was nothing downstream to run away; at 300 steps there is.
acceptance_criteria: A drive is chosen by measurement such that all three arms satisfy readout_live >= 1 and active_fraction <= 0.25 at the 300-step window, recorded as a pre-registered amendment; or the criterion is deliberately relaxed with the arm-dependence argued for in writing.
notes: CORRECTION to this issue's earlier recommendation. Sweeping the drive alone gave [0.20, 0.25], and gradient_reach_v783.json shows what that costs: at drive 0.25 only 1 of 44 readout units moves from rest, spread 0.127 mV, and the encoder gradient is 3800x smaller than at the production drive. That value satisfies the activity ceiling by destroying the signal the readout exists to carry. Mapping the plane instead (operating_point_v783.json): at w_syn 0.138, half the published 0.275, all three arms satisfy the criterion at the production drive of 20.0, with readout live on 11 / 3 / 8 of 44. Four of twenty cells pass, three of them at w_syn 0.138. The binding constraint is always the random arm's active fraction, never the real arm's.

title: Pilot does not fit in 12 GB at the restored window with the pre-registered PPO minibatch
description: Measured on the RTX 4070 Ti: run_pilot --seeds 1 --steps 500 --eval-episodes 5 --only raw reached '[raw] real seed 0' and then ran 28 minutes without completing that seed, ending in CUDA caching-allocator OOM thrash (allocation of 1228931072 bytes refused with free: 0 of total: 12878086144). Graph construction itself is fine and fast: N=15400, |E|=310867, 1042 inputs, 44 outputs in 3.8 s, manifest verified, window correctly reported as 30 ms = 300 steps at drive 20.0. The failing allocation is 300 x 15400 x ~66 float32, i.e. a single BPTT activation tensor for a PPO minibatch, so the binding constraint is memory rather than throughput.
design: The pre-registered train_kwargs recorded in pilot_v783_a4.json are rollout_steps=500, minibatch=32, epochs=4. At the broken 30-step window those fit; at the corrected 300-step window the activation graph is ten times deeper. Options are gradient checkpointing over the rollout, a smaller PPO minibatch, truncated BPTT within the decision window, or a smaller P1 subset -- the last is a protocol amendment, the first three are not.
acceptance_criteria: A documented configuration completes one seed of one arm at 300 steps inside 12 GB, with the deviation from the pre-registered train_kwargs recorded in the result config.
notes: Resolved in practice by two flags rather than by a code fix. With --coupling gather and --minibatch 8 the pilot completes: 3 arms x 1 seed x 300 env steps x 5 eval episodes in 415 s, peaking at about 8.1 GB of the card. The pre-registered minibatch of 32 still raises OutOfMemoryError at the 300-step window, so running at 8 is a deviation, and run_pilot records it in config.train_kwargs. What remains open is whether the deviation is acceptable or whether the window/subset should change instead.

title: No substrate-liveness gate on the path that produces results
description: controls.py defines activity_profile and calibrate_w_syn, which check that at least one readout neuron fires and that the network is not saturated. Verified by repo-wide grep: they are referenced only inside controls.py itself and tests/test_controls.py. experiment.py and run_pilot.py never call them. The production path uses a hardcoded INPUT_DRIVE_MV=20.0 (experiment.py:56) and the ShiuParams default w_syn_mv=0.275 with no per-arm check that anything fires, and ExperimentResult provenance/config record no spike count, active fraction or readout liveness. This substrate has already gone fully silent once (experiment.py:41-49 documents zero neurons firing at drive 0.06) and was caught only by hand.
design: Failure is silent and well-formed: a dead substrate still lets the trainable encoder, heads and low-rank adapter produce gradients, so training completes, evaluation completes, analysis.compare_arms computes a bootstrap CI and Holm-adjusted p over noise, and save_result writes a valid JSON. Nothing raises.
acceptance_criteria: run_seed or make_policy measures per-arm activity before training, records active_fraction and readout_live in provenance, and raises when an arm's readout population is dead.
notes: CORRECTION to the previous note. The 0.811 active fraction reported there was measured by driving the first 1042 positions in sorted root_id order rather than the 1042 neurons select_io_indices returns -- current went into the wrong neurons. Retracted. The correct measurement (data/results/drive_at_window_v783.json, controls.activity_profile with real indices, 300 steps, published w_syn) is: at drive 20.0 the active fraction is 0.1762 for real, 0.2104 for shuffled and 0.6037 for random, against the 0.25 ceiling. So the real and shuffled arms pass and the RANDOM CONTROL fails, at 2.4x the ceiling. The gate is still needed and would still fire -- on the control rather than on the real arm, which is arguably worse for the comparison.

title: Produce the first valid fly-ky7.11 pilot result on HEAD
description: No valid pilot result exists at HEAD. data/results/pilot_v783_a4.json was produced with decision_window_steps=30 -- the broken 3 ms window, at which decision_window_v783.json records zero non-input neurons firing -- and with the per-arm branching calibration that commit 7dd3bd6 later removed as a confound. Its recorded ordering real>shuffled>random is therefore an artefact of that calibration, not of topology: the random arm scored exactly -1.0 on both seeds, i.e. zero wins out of 40 on each. Both causes are fixed at HEAD (a095f35 restored the 30 ms window, 7dd3bd6 removed the calibration) but no run on the corrected code has completed.
design: Two non-code blockers. Budget: decision_window_v783.json records 146 s per fwd+bwd at batch 1 and 300 steps, putting the pre-registered confirmatory series near 4700 h; dt_sensitivity_v783.json closes the coarsening route because dt error is topology-correlated and biased toward the hypothesis under test. Effect size: the amplitude confound that motivated fly-ky7.11 is about 11 percent once per-arm calibration is removed, not the 1400 percent A4 recorded, so a null result is a live possibility and should not be read as failure.
acceptance_criteria: A pilot result file exists whose config records decision_window_steps=300, whose provenance records per-arm substrate liveness, produced by code with this epic's children resolved.
notes: First fly-ky7.11 measurement on HEAD, 2026-09-17 (data/results/ky711_first_measurement_v783.json). Both variants completed with --coupling gather --minibatch 8 at 1 seed, 600 steps, 20 eval episodes: raw 843 s, standardised 924 s. The amplitude ordering real > shuffled > random survives, but the confound does not: median readout s.d. is 0.5468 / 0.5380 / 0.5318, a spread of 2.83 percent, against a factor of fourteen at amendment A4 and a predicted eleven percent at the restored window. Standardisation was real rather than a no-op -- dead units 1, 1 and 0 of 44 -- which is only checkable because the calibration record now reaches provenance. Zero truncated episodes in all six arm-runs. The scores carry no information (raw -1.0 everywhere, standardised -1.0 / -0.9 / -0.9, one win in twenty): at this budget every arm loses every game, so evaluation has no discriminating power. The epic's blocker is now the floor, not the confound.

title: Add a non-connectome baseline sized to our exact trainable-parameter count
description: We have no conventional-network control, so 'the connectome did not help' is currently indistinguishable from 'nothing helped on this task'. None of the three comparable projects does this properly either. eganeganegan/flydoom defines MLP/GRU/LSTM baselines whose file docstring claims 'Conventional actor-critic baselines for parameter-budget matching', but scripts/train.py:286 sizes them from a static baseline_hidden_size: 128 in YAML, unrelated to the connectome subgraph's size. seanphan/flyt3's widely cited result -- pooled-pixel MLP 85.7 percent against the circuit's 60.8 -- cannot be checked for budget matching at all, because the baseline's training code is not in the repository; its own report calls it 'an earlier artifact under this name'.
design: Our trainable set is the rank-8 adapter (2 * 15400 * 8 = 246,400 parameters) plus the encoder and the two heads. Computing that total and sizing an MLP or GRU policy to match it programmatically, rather than to a hand-set default, would be stricter than any of the three precedents. The baseline must see the same observation encoding and train under the same PPO settings and budget, or it is not a control.
acceptance_criteria: A non-connectome policy with a trainable-parameter count matched to the spiking policy's, trained on the same budget, is reported beside the three arms.

title: calibrate_w_syn searches only upward and cannot find the working operating point
description: W_SYN_CANDIDATES is tuple(round(0.275 * 1.5**k, 3) for k in range(11)) at controls.py:284 -- eleven values from the published 0.275 up to about 15.9, none below. The stated reasoning is that a subset retains only a fraction of each neuron's real input, so the workable scale should sit at or above the published value. Measurement on the real P1 subset points the other way: at the production drive the failure is the random arm propagating too much, and the only cells where all three arms satisfy the criterion sit at w_syn 0.138, half the published value (operating_point_v783.json). Every candidate in the current grid makes the random arm worse.
design: The fix is not simply to extend the grid downward, because the criterion is two-sided: lowering w_syn brings the random arm under the activity ceiling but also empties the readout, which is the other clause. calibrate_w_syn already encodes both clauses, so extending the candidates below 0.275 and letting it search is the minimal change. Worth checking at the same time whether the function should be sweeping at a fixed drive at all, given that drive and w_syn trade against each other.
acceptance_criteria: W_SYN_CANDIDATES spans both sides of the published value, calibrate_w_syn is run on the real subset for all three arms, and its chosen scale plus the full sweep reach the run's provenance.

title: Vectorise the environment: rollout collection wastes the card
description: Measured end to end (data/results/end_to_end_budget_v783.json): 0.44 s per env-step per arm, giving 2.2 h for the default pilot and about 1833 h for the pre-registered confirmatory series. The card bought a factor of 2.6 over the M1 Pro estimate of 4700 h, while the rollout benchmark showed 132x at 30 steps. Both are correct and measure different things: the benchmark times one batched forward+backward, whereas a pilot spends most of its time collecting rollouts, and every env decision is a single forward at batch 1 through 300 sequential steps.
design: Batch is nearly free on this substrate -- gather at 300 steps costs 274 ms at batch 1 and 280 ms at batch 8 -- so the card sits idle through rollout collection. Running B games in lockstep and stacking their observations into the batch dimension of one SpikingPolicy.act would convert most of that. The obstacle is that MiniCard is stepped one action at a time and seats alternate, so the vectorised loop has to handle games ending at different times and opponents moving on different turns. Memory is linear in batch, and batch 8 already peaks at 7.5 GB at the full window, so the achievable B on 12 GB is small unless the window is checkpointed.
acceptance_criteria: Rollout collection runs B games in one batched forward, and the measured seconds per env-step per arm falls by close to a factor of B.

title: 705 neurons in the P1 subset carry no transmitter prediction and are silenced
description: Found by the new check on real v783 data: 705 of the 15400 neurons in the P1 subset (4.58 percent) have a null nt_type in neurons.csv.gz. Zero are absent from the table, so the join is intact -- the release simply has no prediction for them. Under Dale's law they are signed 0, which makes every one of their outgoing edges transmit nothing, in all three arms, and makes them indistinguishable from genuinely modulatory neurons.
design: Three options, and the choice is the protocol's rather than the code's. Keep signing them 0, which is the current behaviour and is defensible as 'no known sign, no transmission', but should be stated rather than inherited. Exclude them from the subset, which changes N and the edge count and therefore rule P1. Or impute a sign from the per-edge nt_type prediction in connections.csv.gz, which the module deliberately avoids on the grounds that one neuron cannot be half-excitatory. run_pilot now prints and records the count either way, so whatever is chosen is visible in the run.
acceptance_criteria: The treatment of null-transmitter neurons is stated in the protocol, and the count reaches ExperimentResult provenance.

title: Gradient checkpointing over the rollout is the structural fix for the window cost
description: The 300-step window does not fit on 12 GB because the backward graph stores roughly 300 tensors per step: measured 21.5 MB per step at batch 1, linear in steps, 4291 MB at 200 steps, and a reserved-to-allocated ratio near 2.2 that puts 250 steps over the card. Raising the batch cannot help, since memory is linear in batch as well.
design: torch.utils.checkpoint over segments of LIFSubstrate.rollout recomputes activations during backward instead of storing them, trading roughly a third more time for memory on the order of sqrt(steps) segments. The rollout is a plain Python loop over constant-shape state, which is the easy case to segment: checkpoint every k steps, carrying v, g and refractory across the boundary. refractory is an integer countdown deliberately outside the autograd graph, so it must be passed through rather than recomputed as a differentiable value.
acceptance_criteria: One seed of one arm completes at 300 steps inside 12 GB, with the measured time cost of checkpointing recorded next to the uncheckpointed 200-step figure.
notes: Autograd graph accounting on CPU (n=3000, 60k edges, batch 1, marginal between 5 and 15 steps) refutes the sparse-operand-duplication guess: SparseCooTensorWithDimsAndTensorsBackward0 holds 1.200 MB in exactly ONE tensor at 0.000 MB per step, so the sparse matrix is saved once for the whole rollout, not per step. Marginal saved-tensor cost is 0.096 MB per step for sparse (8x one (1,n) tensor) against 0.564 MB for gather (47x) -- the production default is the memory-efficient one by a factor of six. But scaling the sparse figure to n=15400 predicts about 0.49 MB per step, while the card measured 21.5 MB: a factor of forty unaccounted for. Two known holes in the accounting: SurrogateSpike is a custom autograd.Function whose saved_tensors are not exposed through _saved_* attributes and so are absent from the table entirely, and max_memory_allocated includes backward-pass transients rather than only saved tensors. The composition question is narrower now but still open, and neither checkpointing nor any other remedy should be chosen until it is closed.

title: Measure the batch/throughput ceiling at the restored 30 ms window
description: dt_sensitivity_v783.json closes dt coarsening: the error is topology-correlated and always ordered real>shuffled>random, so it biases toward the hypothesis under test. Of the four remaining budget levers it names -- fewer seeds, shorter per-seed budget, smaller P1 subset, larger GPU batches -- only the last is an implementation question. Sweep batch against hours_per_500k_steps and peak memory on the RTX 4070 Ti (12 GB) at steps=300, one process per configuration so an OOM cannot fragment the allocator for the next one.
acceptance_criteria: A results artifact records, per coupling mode, the largest batch that fits in 12 GB and the implied hours per 5e5 steps.
notes: Partial curve on the 4070 Ti, sparse, batch 1, repeats 1 (data/results/window_cost_v783.json): 30 steps 111.9 ms peak 1183 MB; 60 steps 256.3 ms 1373 MB; 100 steps 492.5 ms 2155 MB; 150 steps 853.3 ms 3223 MB; 200 steps 1279.3 ms 4291 MB. Time and memory are both linear in steps up to 200 (about 21 MB per step), which extrapolates to roughly 6.4 GB at 300 -- comfortably inside 12 GB. Yet the standalone 300-step run did not complete in 600 s and the 250-step point pushed the card to 11.95 GB, so something non-additive happens between 200 and 250 steps. That discontinuity, not the linear cost, is what blocks the restored window.
close_reason: Measured and written up in three artifacts. window_cost_v783.json locates the cliff: sparse is linear to 200 steps (1279 ms, 4291 MB) then fails to finish 250 or 300 in 240 s, and batching is nearly free (56x the work for 14 percent more time at 30 steps). gather_at_window_v783.json answers the budget question differently than expected: gather clears the full 300-step window at 274 ms and 961 MB, batch 8 is the ceiling on 12 GB, batch 16 spills to host memory under WDDM (14926 MB peak on a 12282 MiB card, 12x slower) and batch 32 raises OutOfMemoryError. mode_equivalence_v783.json confirms the modes are byte-identical on the real subset, so the swap is a configuration choice. run_pilot now takes --coupling.

title: Decide and document whether CUDA runs are seed-reproducible
description: No use_deterministic_algorithms, CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG, TF32 setting or cudnn.deterministic anywhere in src/ (verified by grep). The default coupling mode is SPARSE, whose backward uses atomic accumulation on CUDA, so torch.manual_seed pins the draw stream but not the summation order. Two runs with identical CLI args on the same GPU may report different scores for the same declared seed.
acceptance_criteria: Either the confirmatory path enables deterministic algorithms and is shown to reproduce, or the write-up states plainly that GPU runs are not bit-reproducible and says what is pinned instead.

title: calibrate_readout diagnostics are computed then discarded
description: experiment.py:165-168 calls policy.calibrate_readout(...) and drops its return value, which contains n_states, dead_units, mean_abs_mean, median_sd and feature_rms -- exactly the numbers the fly-ky7.11 argument needs. config records only the boolean standardise flag. If an arm's readout collapses to mostly dead units, calibration falls back to scale=1.0 by design and standardisation quietly becomes a no-op for that arm, invisible in the saved result.
acceptance_criteria: Per-arm calibration diagnostics are persisted into ExperimentResult provenance or config.
close_reason: make_policy now attaches the statistics to the policy, run_seed collects them per arm, and run_experiment writes provenance.calibration. Four tests in tests/test_standardise_wiring.py cover the round trip, the empty case on a raw run, and that the record stays out of state_dict.

title: save_result is a non-atomic overwrite that can destroy a completed run
description: experiment.py:329-342 calls Path(path).write_text(...) with no temp file and no os.replace, at a deterministic path built in run_pilot.py:176 from label/release/arm/tag with no existence check. write_text truncates before writing, so an interruption leaves a truncated file, and a rerun with the same --label/--tag silently destroys a previous complete result before writing.
acceptance_criteria: Results are written to a temp file in the same directory and moved into place with os.replace; overwriting an existing complete result requires an explicit flag.
close_reason: Fixed with regression tests in tests/test_result_integrity.py (14 tests): save_result writes to a sibling temp file and os.replace's it into place with fsync, decision_window_steps raises when dt does not divide the 30 ms window, and the release tag in result filenames is derived from connectome.RELEASE_TAG.

title: Action-cap truncation is scored identically to a genuine draw
description: experiment.py:213 sets scores[episode] = float(outcome) if game.is_over else 0.0, and ppo.py:145 does finish(outcome if game.is_over else 0). An episode that hits max_actions (600) is therefore recorded as 0.0, bit-identical to a real draw, and no counter or field anywhere records how many episodes were truncated versus concluded.
design: A policy that cycles through legal non-terminating actions would fill an arm with 0.0 scores; compare_arms would report a clean null result that is actually a mechanical hang. Second instance of degenerate-result laundering in this codebase.
acceptance_criteria: Truncated episodes are counted separately from draws and the count reaches ExperimentResult.provenance.
close_reason: evaluate_policy now counts episodes cut off by the action cap into an optional sink; run_seed and run_experiment thread it into provenance.truncated_episodes per arm and seed. Three tests in tests/test_result_integrity.py, including that a cap of one action truncates every episode and that the sink stays optional.

title: dale_signs silently maps missing or unknown transmitters to sign 0
description: connectome.py:191-196 returns _DALE_SIGN.get(lookup.get(rid), 0) -- two chained silent defaults. A root_id present in the connectome subset but absent from neurons.csv.gz yields None then 0; any transmitter string outside the six in _DALE_SIGN also yields 0. Sign 0 is indistinguishable from a genuine modulatory neuron. run_pilot.py:74 passes a Series indexed by root_id with no reindex or coverage check against the neuron ids.
design: A wrongly-zeroed sign silences every outgoing edge of that neuron in all three arms, since build_arms shares the sign vector unmodified, and it pollutes the modulatory count in controls.graph_stats into a mix of real modulatory neurons and join gaps.
acceptance_criteria: Unmatched root_ids and unknown transmitter categories are counted and reported; the run aborts above a stated tolerance instead of defaulting to 0.
close_reason: dale_signs now separates the two failures that both collapsed into a silent 0: a neuron absent from the transmitter table, and a transmitter category outside Dale's six. It counts them, names the unknown categories in the message, and raises ManifestMismatch above a tolerance. The library default is permissive (max_unsigned_fraction=1.0) so the documented mapping and its existing five-neuron test are untouched; run_pilot passes MAX_UNSIGNED_FRACTION=0.01 explicitly, because the strictness belongs on the path whose output is evidence. Six tests in tests/test_run_pilot_wiring.py.

title: Declare the held-out evaluation seeds as pre-registered
description: Our evaluation seeds are derived as seed * 100_003 + episode while training games use seed + iteration * 1000 + episode, so the two spaces are disjoint by construction. That disjointness is an implementation detail nobody has written down as a protocol commitment, and a reviewer cannot tell it from a coincidence. cobanov/flyjump names its test seeds explicitly (2100001-2100100, 'absent from training and validation', 'Architecture and weights were frozen before this test', docs/experiment.md:82).
acceptance_criteria: The evaluation seed range is stated in the protocol as held out, and the result file records that the policy was frozen before evaluation.

title: Beads has no Dolt remote, so issue history is stranded per-machine
description: bd dolt pull fails with 'no remote'. The database on this Windows host was empty until now, while fly-ky7.11 and fly-4s8 -- referenced in code comments and in two xfail(strict=True) markers -- exist only on the macOS dev host and were never synced. Issue ids cited in source therefore cannot be resolved from this machine.
acceptance_criteria: A Dolt remote is configured against the git remote and the two hosts' issue databases are reconciled.

title: The standardise=True orchestration path is never exercised by a test
description: grep finds no test calling run_experiment( or run_seed(. Standardisation is covered only at the SpikingPolicy.calibrate_readout unit level in tests/test_amplitude_control.py, so a wiring bug in the standardise pass-through added to run_seed/run_experiment would not be caught. The new config keys decision_window_ms and standardise are likewise never produced by a test -- the round-trip tests build config by hand.
acceptance_criteria: One integration test calls run_experiment(standardise=True) on the synthetic fixture and asserts the config keys it should have written.
close_reason: Covered by tests/test_standardise_wiring.py (5 tests): the flag is asserted at make_policy and through run_experiment, the default is pinned to raw, and decision_window_ms is checked against dt.

title: run_pilot.py has zero test coverage
description: grep run_pilot tests/ returns nothing. All 193 lines of the CUDA entry point are untested: manifest wiring, the root_id-to-position mapping, label alignment through select_io_indices, --only/--label/--tag handling, the variants loop and the output path construction. The suite runs entirely on synthetic fixtures and never touches data/raw, so a green run says nothing about whether build_real_graph works on the real 15,400-node subset.
acceptance_criteria: build_real_graph and main are covered with tmp_path fixtures and monkeypatched loaders, without touching real data or training.
close_reason: tests/test_run_pilot_wiring.py (7 tests) covers build_real_graph with monkeypatched loaders: the manifest is verified before any table is read, a ManifestMismatch stops the run with nothing loaded, labels reach select_io_indices as a positional array in neuron order rather than as a root_id-indexed Series, edges are remapped to positions in sorted-id order, Dale signs are requested in that same order, and pick_device honours an explicit request.

title: Release tag v783 is hardcoded into result filenames and never checked
description: run_pilot.py:176 builds the output filename with a literal v783, duplicating connectome.RELEASE without importing or comparing it. verify_manifest checks file hashes, not the release string, and provenance records only per-file sha256s. Repinning data/manifest.json to a different FlyWire release would keep producing files named v783 with no error.
acceptance_criteria: The filename derives from connectome.RELEASE, or the run fails when the two disagree.
close_reason: Fixed with regression tests in tests/test_result_integrity.py (14 tests): save_result writes to a sibling temp file and os.replace's it into place with fsync, decision_window_steps raises when dt does not divide the 30 ms window, and the release tag in result filenames is derived from connectome.RELEASE_TAG.

title: decision_window_steps rounds without asserting the window is preserved
description: experiment.py:74-80 returns round(DECISION_WINDOW_MS / dt_ms) with no check that the division is exact. Correct today (30.0/0.1 = 300), but a future dt that does not divide 30 ms evenly drifts the window silently -- the same class of failure the surrounding docstring says this design prevents. It prevents the old hardcoded-step-count bug, not this one.
acceptance_criteria: decision_window_steps raises when abs(steps*dt_ms - DECISION_WINDOW_MS) exceeds a stated epsilon.
close_reason: Fixed with regression tests in tests/test_result_integrity.py (14 tests): save_result writes to a sibling temp file and os.replace's it into place with fsync, decision_window_steps raises when dt does not divide the 30 ms window, and the release tag in result filenames is derived from connectome.RELEASE_TAG.

title: Test whether expandable_segments lifts the 250-step allocator cliff
description: Measured on the 4070 Ti at batch 1, sparse, one repeat: 200 steps costs 1279 ms and peaks at 4291 MB allocated, while 250 steps does not finish in 240 s and drives the card to 11.9 GB as reported by nvidia-smi. Time and memory are both linear up to 200 steps (about 21 MB per step), so 250 should cost roughly 1.6 s and 5.3 GB. It does not. The gap between 4.3 GB allocated and 11.9 GB resident is the signature of caching-allocator fragmentation: reserved segments cannot be reused for a differently sized request, the allocator hits the limit, frees its cache, retries, and thrashes.
design: Corrected reasoning after reading LIFSubstrate.rollout: every per-step tensor has the constant shape (batch, n) and the raster is accumulated in a Python list and stacked once at the end. Uniformly sized allocations are the caching allocator's best case, so 'fragmentation from varying shapes' is the wrong diagnosis. The arithmetic that does fit: 4291 MB allocated at 200 steps is 21.5 MB per step against a 61.6 KB (1, 15400) tensor, i.e. roughly 300 tensors saved per step for backward, since each lerp, clamp and maximum saves its inputs. nvidia-smi read 11.9 GB during the 250-step run against an expected 5.4 GB allocated, a reserved-to-allocated ratio near 2.2 -- and at 250 steps that ratio puts reserved into the 12.28 GB card. expandable_segments is still worth one cheap measurement, but it moves the wall at best.
acceptance_criteria: The 250 and 300 step points are measured with and without expandable_segments, and the result is recorded in data/results/window_cost_v783.json.
notes: Largely moot now that gather clears the window at 961 MB. Worth keeping only for the case where sparse is required for some other reason, and downgraded accordingly. Note also that the fragmentation framing in the original description was wrong: the batch-16 measurement (14926 MB peak on a 12282 MiB card) points at a WDDM host-memory spill rather than at allocator fragmentation, and graph accounting showed the sparse matrix is saved once per rollout rather than per step.
